title: Epoch Bridge and Proactive Regeneration for Tenant Quota Continuity
creator: Aditi Raman
description:
Problem: Tenants experience small but visible billing/usage artifacts during epoch boundaries (daily/monthly/rolling) and during reserved-capacity cutovers between pools/regions. These artifacts include short double-count windows, brief service denials due to lease handoff races, and ambiguous prorated allowances after a migration or timezone shift.

Background: We have many ad-hoc fixes (midnight cutover safe steps, soft rollforward) but no single coordinated service to ensure continuity across: - tenant timezone changes - reserved pool migrations - rolling window boundaries (sliding vs fixed) - DST and leap-second edge cases - cross-pool quota transfers

Proposed solution: Introduce an "Epoch Bridge" microservice plus a Proactive Regeneration workflow. The Epoch Bridge is a lightweight coordinator that: 1) subscribes to tenant epoch events (reset schedules, pool transfers, timezone updates) 2) computes a short-lived pro-rated allowance token (bridge token) that represents safe credit to be consumed during the handoff window 3) orchestrates a deterministic rollforward or rollback plan for quota ledgers when late events are detected 4) emits reconciliations and compensated ledger ops for the billing ledger so invoices/usage align with customer-facing counters

The Proactive Regeneration workflow: - periodically precomputes next-epoch consumption projections for high-variance tenants and pre-allocates ephemeral burst credit when predicted traffic intersects the epoch boundary - triggers rebalancing for reserved accounts that are scheduled for pool migration in the next N minutes

Implementation details: - Data model: bridge token is an opaque identifier mapped to a small ledger delta stored in Redis with 30-120s TTL; persistent audit written to the primary usage ledger for later reconciliation - API: public internal endpoints: /bridge/prepare, /bridge/commit, /bridge/abort, /bridge/status - Consistency model: optimistic handoff with idempotent commit/abort semantics. Use lease fencing and monotonic sequence numbers from the existing quota ledger to avoid double-apply - Telemetry: expose metrics for bridge token issuance rate, consumer hit/miss, reconciliation delta distribution, and invoice adjustments emitted - Backfill: support late-event backfills by emitting compensating ledger entries and a reconciliation flag that informs billing export - Operational: circuit-breaker that disables proactive regen during heavy congestion; visual dashboard in Console for active bridge windows

Tradeoffs considered: - Using longer-lived tokens (minutes) reduces races but increases exposure to accidental overuse; chose 30-120s TTL with pool-configurable max tokens per tenant - Synchronous commit to billing ledger increases latency; will use async write with a durable append and acknowledgement cohort to keep API latency bounded

Rollout plan: 1) Internal dry-run mode: Issuance-only (no effect on billing) for 2 weeks for 5% traffic 2) Shadow write mode: create ledger entries but mark them as 'bridge.shadow' for 1 week and validate invoices 3) Controlled enablement: enable commit for opt-in customers and reserved accounts 4) Full rollout after 4 weeks of stable metrics

Backout plan: - feature flag to mute bridge issuance - automatic abort under reconciliation error thresholds - revert flows to allow legacy midnight-safe-cutover path

Notes on quota types covered: - rolling-window free tiers - monthly reserved capacity allocations - per-route ephemeral burst buckets

Security & compliance: bridge tokens are ephemeral; all audit entries written to immutable ledger and KMS-encrypted export for finance audits
acceptance_criteria: Bridge service issues tokens and tokens are consumed exactly-once (idempotent commit semantics verified)
No increase in 5xx errors during issuance dry-run (2% threshold beyond baseline)
Billing ledger contains audit records for every bridge commit/abort and reconciliations are applied to exports
Reserved-capacity migrations using bridge show <0.1% customer-facing throttles during cutover windows in staged tests
Prometheus dashboards for token rate, reconciliation delta, and shadow-write discrepancies are live and validated
tasks: Design data schema for bridge token and reconciliation flags in ledger
Integrate optimistic lease fencing with quota ledger sequence numbers
Add shadow-write path in billing export and wire up reconciliation flags
Create proactive regen scheduler and prediction heuristic for high-variance tenants
Build Console dashboard and feature flag controls
Run canary: 5% traffic dry-run then 20% shadow-write, analyze metrics
Update runbook and incident playbook for bridge failures
notes: Prediction heuristic: start with last-7-day epoch-aligned traffic and exponential smoothing; refine with anomaly detection in later cycles
Default bridge TTL = 60s; configurable per-tenant via reserved-capacity profile
Keep bridge token usage cheap: chargeable ledger entries created only on commit
Edge case: cross-account transfer where both accounts are moving epoch windows requires two-phase commit - defer to v2
We will reuse existing exported billing schema with an added field 'bridge_context' to avoid downstream changes
